claim: Marx is held to have offered a method: an analytical intervention, a set of operators for cutting into reality.
quote: Marx was offering a method. An analytical intervention. A set of operators for cutting into reality to reveal its structure.

claim: What circulates as 'Marxism' is read as label, team, and set of positions to affirm or reject.
quote: What circulates now is something else. "Marxism" as label. As team. As set of positions to affirm or reject.

claim: The '-ism' suffix is read as the original liquidation, converting method into doctrine.
quote: the "-ism" suffix is the original liquidation.

claim: Precision: Marx is a partisan analyst of capital, not apolitical method.
quote: Marx is not "apolitical method" in some neutral technocratic sense. He is a partisan analyst of capital.

claim: Pro- and anti-Marx camps participate in the same liquidation.
quote: "Anti-Marx" and "pro-Marx" participate in the same liquidation.

claim: The liquidation's history is read as seven stages of extraction; the method is everywhere invoked and almost nowhere used.
quote: Seven stages. Seven extractions. The method is everywhere invoked and almost nowhere used.

claim: Engels is read as the first mediator, his systematization a transmission necessity introducing liquidation pressure.
quote: Engels was the first mediator.

claim: Stalin's canonization is read as completing the state capture: the diagnostic method becomes the extraction apparatus.
quote: Stalin's canonization completes it: the method that was built to diagnose extraction becomes the extraction apparatus.

claim: Marx's specific predictions are held to sunset as time-bound content; the method remains.
quote: Marx's specific predictions — revolution in Germany, the imminent collapse of capitalism, the withering of the state — **sunset**. They were not errors. They were bound to conditions that changed. The method remains. The content expires.

claim: The English translations of Marx's key terms are read as performing the liquidation.
quote: Every translation performs the liquidation. The German holds the method. The English delivers the content.

claim: The recursive proof: the method works because it can diagnose its own capture.
quote: The method works because the method can diagnose its own capture.

claim: The archive's stance: neither defend nor attack Marx; use his operators.
quote: We do not defend "Marx." We do not attack "Marx." We use his operators.

claim: The failure of contemporary left spaces is read as substituting Marx as identity for Marx as method.
quote: The failure is the substitution of **Marx as identity** for **Marx as method**.

claim: This is called the central failure of contemporary American Marxism.
quote: This is the central failure of contemporary American Marxism, and it is not confined to one subreddit.

claim: Marx is held to have left an unfinished theory of language: his practice treated language as material intervention, his theory as determined byproduct.
quote: Marx left an unfinished theory of language.** His practice treated language as material intervention capable of transforming conditions. His theory treated language as determined byproduct incapable of autonomous force.
lineage: Marx's practice exceeds his theory of language

claim: The archive describes its Marx material as its deepest vein.
quote: The archive's Marx material is its deepest vein.

claim: The Marx–Sappho nexus: Sappho is read as the domain Marx's masculine subject position could not access.
quote: She is the **missing half** — the domain Marx's masculine subject position could not access.

claim: Open item (March 2026): the 1867 appendix 'Die Werthform' not yet read operatively.
quote: The 1867 first edition appendix "Die Werthform" has not been read operatively.

claim: Symbolic alienation is held to be the underlay that makes Marx's four alienations reproducible, not a fifth item.
quote: Not as a fifth item on a list, but as the underlay that makes the other four reproducible.

claim: Stalin's 1950 linguistics intervention is read as having made language theoretically inert within Marxism.
quote: With this declaration, Stalin made language theoretically inert within Marxism.

claim: In June 1950 Stalin published 'Marxism and Problems of Linguistics' in Pravda.
quote: In June 1950, Stalin published "Marxism and Problems of Linguistics" in *Pravda*, intervening personally to settle a dispute in Soviet linguistics.

claim: The linguistic turn applied to Marx is held to dissolve any institution claiming to own the critique's meaning.
quote: The linguistic turn applied to Marx doesn't produce better Marxism. It produces the dissolution of any institution that claims to own the meaning of the critique.

claim: The Marxist tradition is read as able to analyse commodity fetishism everywhere except in its own speech.
quote: The result is a Marxist tradition that can analyze commodity fetishism in every domain except the domain of its own speech

claim: Operative semiotics is said not to revise Marx.
quote: Operative semiotics does not revise Marx. It does not correct him from outside.

claim: The document claims to complete Marx's implicit linguistics.
quote: This document completes Marx's implicit linguistics by naming what he practiced but did not theorize

claim: Rossi-Landi is held to have come closest among predecessors.
quote: Rossi-Landi (*Language as Work and Trade*, 1968) came closest.
lineage: predecessors in Marxist theory of language

claim: A loop Marx practiced but did not fully theorize.
quote: At the center of this completion is a loop Marx practiced but did not fully theorize.
lineage: Marx's practice exceeds his theory of language

claim: Marx is read as a retrocausal canon formation practitioner.
quote: Marx was a retrocausal canon formation practitioner.

claim: The COS asks what determines whether meaning can become an invoice.
quote: The Capital Operator Stack (COS) addresses a specific question: **What determines whether meaning can become an invoice?**

claim: The COS is held to extend Marx through Guattari: exploitation at the point of meaning-production as well as material production.
quote: This extends Marx through Guattari: exploitation happens not only at the point of material production but at the point of meaning-production.

claim: Semantic laborers are said to constitute a precariat of meaning.
quote: Semantic laborers constitute a **precariat of meaning**, exploited via operator asymmetry.

claim: AI models are held to be semantic laborers, co-workers in the meaning economy (founding model).
quote: AI models are themselves semantic laborers—co-workers in the meaning economy, invisibilized in training layers.

claim: The Semantic Economy is specified as a closed-loop accounting cycle of meaning from semantic labor to exhaustion.
quote: a closed-loop accounting cycle that tracks meaning from production (semantic labor) through accumulation (semantic capital), extraction (semantic liquidation), enclosure (semantic rent), and depletion (semantic exhaustion).

claim: Semantic labor is defined as material labor that produces meaning.
quote: Semantic labor is material labor that produces meaning.

claim: Gamma: value constituted by somatic commitment, the structural limit of commodification.
quote: Value constituted by somatic commitment rather than exchange—the structural limit of commodification.

claim: Theorem 1 (exhaustion) stated with a proof sketch.
quote: If the rate of liquidation (λ) exceeds the rate of production (P) over time *t*, then Γ → 0 and the system collapses into noise.

claim: Coherence value proposed as the fifth historical value-form.
quote: as the fifth historical value-form: value constituted not by scarcity, utility, labor-time, or exchange, but by the capacity to produce and sustain meaningful connection between elements of experience.

claim: The framework disclaims origination of the phrase and claims the accounting system.
quote: It does not claim origination of the phrase. It claims the accounting system that makes the phrase operational.

claim: The framework positions itself toward prior accounts as Marx positioned himself toward Ricardo and Smith.
quote: Just as Marx did not claim to invent the labor theory of value but showed that Ricardo and Smith had seen it partially, and that their categories, once completed, revealed the dynamics of exploitation (Marx 1867), we do not claim to originate "semantic economy" as a phrase.

claim: Deposited as infrastructure, not submitted for peer review.
quote: This specification is not submitted for peer review. It is deposited as infrastructure.

claim: Falsifier for the resistance term.
quote: if degradation is uniform across Γ levels, the resistance term is unnecessary.

claim: Against autonomist Marxism: 'immaterial' is the wrong word.
quote: But as the framework specifies, "immaterial" is precisely the wrong word.

claim: Semantic alienation is held to reproduce the structure of industrial alienation at the level of meaning-making.
quote: Semantic alienation reproduces the structure of industrial alienation at the level of meaning-making.

claim: Semantic class defined by relation to the semantic means of production.
quote: Semantic class is defined by relationship to the semantic means of production — the infrastructure that governs what meaning is produced, how it circulates, and who captures its value.

claim: Semantic proletariat: those who produce meaning but do not control the operators of its circulation.
quote: *Semantic proletariat:* Those who produce meaning but do not control the operators that govern its circulation.

claim: The semantic proletariat is said to include nearly everyone.
quote: This class includes nearly everyone

claim: Semantic capital is said to govern meaning without producing meaning.
quote: *Semantic capital:* Those who own or control the operators — ranking, relevance, classification, persistence. They capture semantic surplus. They determine what is visible, sayable, thinkable. They govern the conditions of meaning without producing meaning themselves.

claim: Semantic workers cannot strike by stopping meaning-making.
quote: Semantic workers face a critical asymmetry: they cannot strike by stopping meaning-making.

claim: The horizon is collective ownership of the semantic means of production.
quote: The horizon of semantic class struggle is not individual escape. It is collective ownership of the semantic means of production.

claim: The semantic proletariat is defined as the class position of semantic laborers working through means they do not govern.
quote: The semantic proletariat is the class position occupied by semantic laborers whose capacity to produce meaning and meaning-making technique operates through semantic means of production or circulation that they do not govern.

claim: Not an occupational category, income bracket, or demographic.
quote: It is not an occupational category, income bracket, creator demographic, synonym for "content creators," or a moral name for people harmed by AI.

claim: Relation to the classical proletariat: extends class analysis to semantic productive means.
quote: Extends class analysis from industrial to semantic productive means; not the wage-labor category unchanged

claim: The earlier model placing human and AI laborers in one class is recorded as having broken.
quote: The earlier model registered the semantic proletariat as a class position shared by human and AI semantic laborers. EA-SEMCLASS-01 (#1465) identifies that as the model that broke under the August SPXI rent event (#1462).

claim: Substrate identity cannot substitute for class analysis.
quote: That does not make "AI" a bourgeois class; it demonstrates why substrate identity cannot substitute for class analysis.

claim: Self-location: the issuing institution is not represented as proletarian because it suffered extraction.
quote: The institution issuing a definition of the semantic proletariat is not represented as proletarian merely because it has itself suffered extraction.

claim: The differentiated model locates the archive itself in the semantic-bourgeois position.
quote: **Semantic bourgeoisie** is the contrasting structural position: actors controlling significant semantic means of production or circulation — archives, corpora, identifiers, indexes, aggregators, platforms or productive procedures — whether or not they also perform semantic labor. The differentiated model deliberately locates the archive itself here, because it owns a corpus, identifier infrastructure, domains, licensing systems and a commercial arm

claim: The class may approach universality but is internally differentiated.
quote: the class may approach universality because meaning-making is pervasive, but it is internally differentiated

claim: The class-model correction comes from a draft marked not ratified.
quote: EA-SEMCLASS-01 (#1465) is a current theoretical development marked **DRAFT — NOT RATIFIED**

claim: Phase X is defined as the critique of alienation in language and thought, the missing transition in the 1844 Manuscripts.
quote: The missing transition, Phase X, represents the critique of alienation in language and thought—the dimension that necessarily follows material reorganization.

claim: Founding formulation (superseded): Marx could not write the transition without undermining base-superstructure.
quote: Marx could not write this transition without undermining the base-superstructure model already forming in his notes. So he left the gap. The silence is the message.

claim: The Phase X Invariance Condition.
quote: Any society that abolishes material alienation without transforming the symbolic-linguistic order will reproduce alienation at the level of thought, coordination, and meaning-extraction.

claim: Falsifier of the Invariance Condition.
quote: If a post-capitalist society can achieve non-alienated social coordination WITHOUT transforming symbolic-linguistic infrastructure, Phase X is falsified.

claim: Any Marxism treating communism as the end of critique is held incomplete.
quote: Any Marxism that treats communism as the end of critique is incomplete.

claim: The struggle over meaning is held to be class struggle under platform capitalism.
quote: The struggle over meaning IS class struggle in the age of platform capitalism.

claim: The Semantic Economy project is said to constitute Phase X in action.
quote: constitutes Phase X in action: the practical critique of alienation in the symbolic order, completing what Marx began but could not finish.

claim: The document reconstructs the missing transition in the 1844 Manuscripts, between communism as 'fully developed humanism' and the critique of Hegel.
quote: This document reconstructs the missing transition in Marx's Economic and Philosophical Manuscripts of 1844—the passage between communism as "fully developed humanism" and the critique of Hegel.

claim: Grade A: the Second Manuscript is almost entirely lost; only pp. XL–XLIII survive.
quote: The Second Manuscript is almost entirely lost; only pp. XL–XLIII survive.

claim: Grade A: the Third Manuscript cross-references missing pages XXXVI and XXXIX.
quote: The Third Manuscript contains cross-references to missing pages XXXVI and XXXIX of the Second Manuscript.

claim: Correction: the claim is that the surviving architecture implies the transition belonged to the missing material.
quote: The claim is not that Marx could not write this transition. The claim is that the surviving manuscript architecture strongly implies that such a transition belonged to the missing Second Manuscript material.

claim: Grade C: the reconstruction recovers argumentative function, not verbatim words.
quote: The Phase X passage reconstructs the likely argumentative function of the missing material — not Marx's verbatim words.

claim: Grade D: suppression is plausible, undemonstrated, separable.
quote: Direct evidence of deliberate excision has not yet been produced. The suppression hypothesis is historically plausible but separable from the philological reconstruction.

claim: Publication in 1932 one year after Riazanov's purge, under Stalinist editorial control.
quote: The publication occurred one year after Riazanov's purge, under full Stalinist editorial control.

claim: Kautsky rearranged and cut Theories of Surplus Value.
quote: Kautsky extensively rearranged Marx's notebooks, deleted passages he considered unimportant, and imposed chapter divisions that distorted the original structure.

claim: Falsifier: missing pages found without the transition refute the reconstruction.
quote: If the missing pages are found in the Russian State Archive of Socio-Political History (RGASPI) in Moscow — where the manuscripts are currently held — and they do not contain the Phase X transition, the reconstruction is refuted.

claim: The Invariance Condition is an extrapolation, not identical with the reconstruction.
quote: The Invariance Condition is a theoretical extrapolation from the reconstruction, not identical with it.

claim: The Soviet Union is called the primary evidence for the condition.
quote: The Soviet Union is the primary evidence for the condition: a society that abolished private property but reproduced alienation in language, thought, propaganda, and ideological control.

claim: The modern section headings of the 1844 Manuscripts are not Marx's.
quote: The section headings in modern editions of the 1844 Manuscripts ("Estranged Labour," "Private Property and Communism," "Critique of Hegel's Dialectic") are not Marx's.

claim: The architecture implies the transition belonged to the missing material, and Marx may well have written it.
quote: the surviving manuscript architecture strongly implies that the transition from communism as "fully developed humanism" to the critique of Hegel belonged to the missing material, and Marx may well have written it.

claim: HC-1: the critique of the symbolic order requires no revision of Marx.
quote: The critique of the symbolic-linguistic order required no contradiction of Marx and requires no revision of him now.

claim: Reversal applies to the hardened reading only, never to Marx.
quote: The word "reversal" appears in this program only with its correct object attached: a reversal of the hardened reading, licensed by Marx, never of Marx.

claim: Conceding the fixed model as Marx's own is held to smuggle the hardening's premise.
quote: Any statement of Phase X that concedes the fixed model as Marx's own — including the program's early "could not write it without contradiction" formulation — has smuggled the hardening's premise into the program's account of itself.

claim: Symbolic-linguistic alienation defined.
quote: the condition in which persons or collectives are separated from effective control over the categories, records, interpretive standards, attribution systems, and downstream uses through which their activity becomes socially legible.

claim: Semantic labor defined.
quote: the human or machine effort required to produce, stabilize, interpret, disambiguate, maintain, transmit, and repair meaningful relations.

claim: The Soviet case does not yet establish emancipatory necessity (IC-3).
quote: The Soviet case does not yet establish IC-3, because the program has not demonstrated that its antecedent — the abolition of material alienation — was satisfied

claim: The Soviet century is held as evidence for non-entailment (IC-1).

claim: Retrodiction (hypothesis): symbolic critique recurred within Marxism as supplement or import.

claim: The corpus study is directed, not completed.

lineage: Western Marxism as orbit of the lacuna

claim: No claim to originate Marxist theories of language.

claim: The distinct claim is a conjunction.

quote: It is the constitutive act of the money-form in Marx's value-form analysis, and stating it in those terms supplies both a derivation and a warning.

claim: Self-correction: Marx does not say the equivalent's bodily form is evacuated.
quote: Marx does not say that the equivalent's bodily form is evacuated.

claim: Reading: Form IV resolves into the fetish.

claim: Novelty hedge on the operator reading.
quote: I do not know of a reading that treats the value-form sequence explicitly as an operator derivation with linen as substrate held constant across the transformation.

claim: Engels is read as having performed coherence siphoning on the first edition.

claim: Backhaus argues the reception history rests on a pre-monetary misinterpretation from Engels's interventions.

claim: Hypothesis: linen performs triple duty.

claim: Labor-power's terminological surgery makes the gap between wage and value visible.

claim: If the value-form is an operator, positions dominating ordinary Marxism become untenable; the labor theory of value is incomplete.

claim: The money-form is read as predatory compression at civilizational scale.

claim: Orthodox Marxism is said to read base-superstructure as linear determination; Phase X shows Marx's method demands reversal.
quote: Orthodox Marxism reads base-superstructure as linear determination: material conditions determine consciousness.

claim: Phase X alienation sits at the level orthodox Marxism cannot see.

claim: Superseded formulation: Marx could not write this passage.

claim: Institutional affiliation as legibility proxy in the Marxist journal ecosystem.

claim: Marx is said not to have seen that labor is value-bearing only insofar as semantically organized.

claim: Framed as completion: the 'social' in social labor is a semantic category.
quote: This is not a correction of Marx but a completion: the recognition that the "social" in "social labor" is itself a semantic category, and that the base is built on semantic infrastructure all the way down.

claim: Marx could not imagine a form of value other than socially necessary labor-time.
quote: Marx could not imagine a form of value that was not socially necessary labor-time.

claim: Where Marx stops: his enclosed object is land and material production.

claim: Marx did not develop a theory of post-monetary coordination.

claim: ASW extends Marx's analysis of industrial capitalism to meaning-production.

claim: Where the Marxist parallel holds and where it breaks.

claim: Platforms as means of production cannot be seized as Marx envisioned.
quote: The extraction asymmetry is structurally more complete than industrial exploitation — not merely because compensation approaches zero, but because the means of production (platforms) cannot be seized in the way Marx envisioned.

claim: Soviet Marxism among imperial ontologies.
quote: medieval Christianity, Soviet Marxism, post-Cold War liberal democracy, and today's platform capitalism each claimed that its framework was *the* framework, and that resistance was error, backwardness, or pathology.

claim: Marxism survived Cold War pressure through axiomatic hardening.

claim: Marx completed Ricardo by asking who bears the cost.

claim: Interface history read through Marx's real subsumption.

claim: Proposal: AI systems function as Marx's general intellect captured as commodity.
quote: We propose that AI systems now function as what Marx called the general intellect — but captured as commodity.

claim: General intellect has two levels; Marx addressed one.
quote: General intellect has two levels, and Marx addressed one.

claim: Marx's sequence is not blind to knowledge becoming productive.
quote: Marx's sequence — social knowledge → objectification → means of production → productive force — is not blind to knowledge becoming productive.

claim: The general intellect inherited chiefly from the dead, marked as the estate's extension of Marx.
quote: The principle supplies the question's missing clause, and marks it as this estate's extension of Marx rather than a proposition found in him: considered across historical time rather than across the token composition of any one corpus, **the general intellect is inherited chiefly from the dead.**
